name: Typography Contrast Hierarchy Stack
use_when: A hook, title, caption, or graphic needs one word to carry the viewer's attention.
Text looks flat because every word has the same visual priority.
The agent needs to build hierarchy without adding more footage or effects.
avoid_when: Every word is being emphasized because the editor has not chosen the actual point.
The line is serious testimony where dramatic visual emphasis would feel manipulative.
The visual background already carries the idea more clearly than text styling.

timeline_pattern.pattern: line_or_claim -> choose_impact_word -> base_style -> weight_contrast -> optional_hue -> optional_case_change -> optional_size_change -> mix_only_needed_rules -> qc
timeline_pattern.impact_word_rule: Highlight the word that creates the meaning, result, contrast, or emotional punch in the line.
timeline_pattern.weight_rule: Use a noticeable weight jump, such as regular to bold or bold to extra-bold, instead of tiny adjacent changes.
timeline_pattern.color_rule: Use color to mark meaning, contrast, or category; avoid random color changes.
timeline_pattern.case_rule: Use mixed case or all caps only when it improves hierarchy and does not reduce readability.
timeline_pattern.size_rule: Make the most important word visibly larger only when the layout still reads as one sentence.

motion.rule: Animate the hierarchy so the viewer sees support words first or together, then the impact word lands clearly.

keyframe_values.impact_limit: Prefer one primary impact word or phrase per text moment.
keyframe_values.accent_color_limit: Use no more than two accent colors in one text system; neutral white/black/gray can support the layout.
keyframe_values.entrance: For short-form hooks, establish the hierarchy inside the first 1-5 seconds.

sound.rule: Use a subtle hit only on the impact word if the motion and spoken emphasis also land there.

captions.rule: Caption emphasis should follow the spoken meaning; avoid highlighting filler words or every adjective.

color.rule: Accent color should increase meaning and contrast. Gradients are allowed only when edge readability remains better than plain text would be.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use separate drawtext layers for support text and impact text so size, color, weight, and timing can differ.
implementation.remotion: Store impactWords with hierarchyLevel, fontWeight, fontSizeScale, caseMode, accentColor, and timing fields.
implementation.blender: Use separate text objects for hierarchy words and test readability from the final camera.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Split the text into layers, use bold/size/color on the impact word, and check the full phone-size layout.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics text layers or upgraded captions, then style only the impact word or phrase with weight, color, case, or size.

common_mistakes: Making every word bold, big, colored, or uppercase.
Highlighting filler words instead of the word that changes impact.
Using adjacent font weights that do not create visible contrast.
Adding gradients, glow, or shadow before the hierarchy is clear.
Using too many accent colors in one text moment.
qc: Can the viewer identify the impact word immediately?
Does the emphasis match the spoken meaning?
Are support words still readable but lower priority?
Do weight, hue, case, and size choices work together instead of competing?
Does the hierarchy remain readable at phone size?
